body:
## Summary

This PR fixes correctness bugs in `StaticBitVector`, `NamedTuple` output promotion, reductions, and compiler recursion limits; makes sums and products widen `Bool`s and small integers as `Base` does; reduces compilation time; speeds up `StaticBitVector` operations; propagates `@inbounds` to iterator indexing; documents every exported function and adds a cookbook, a page on compilation limits, and an API reference to the documentation; and moves the benchmarks behind an opt-in flag so that each CI job takes 7–16 minutes instead of 34–53. Nothing is breaking, so the last commit cuts the patch release 0.1.12 (see "Release" below). The current revision folds the responses to the review comments into the commits they belong to (see "Review comments" below).

## Review guide

Nine commits, best read in order. Each commit is self-contained and passes the full test suite on its own. The first two only change tests and CI, so the package changes in commits 3–8 are tested with a suite that already runs on CUDA.jl 6 and finishes in minutes.

1. [`aa02501`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/aa0250101d1c5a4b0fa3bf4fdb0be487225c361f) **test: CUDA.jl 6 and PrettyTables 3.** No package code changes. `Project.toml` and `docs/Project.toml` bound `PrettyTables` to `"3"`, which CUDATools 6 (a dependency of CUDA.jl 6) requires; the other test dependencies keep no compat entries, and `test/aqua.jl` keeps `check_extras = false` as on `main`.  `test/test_and_analyze.jl` ports the comparison-table printer to the v3 API. In `test/compilation_limits.jl`, the `runtime_int` helper converts with `unsafe_trunc`, so the 7 `gpu_broken` flags can go (see "Test dependencies" below). The file also accepts the `print_to_string` error that GPUCompiler 2 reports on Julia 1.10, and it discards the LLVM log messages emitted during GPU compilation, because logging from inside codegen can deadlock.
2. [`81e5e55`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/81e5e557239644af87e7dd4a623ba8f92ac793eb) **ci: opt-in benchmarks, workflow updates.** Read `test/test_and_analyze.jl` (the `benchmark_mode` branch in `@test_unrolled`), `test/runtests.jl`, and the three workflows. Documentation builds, including pull request previews, always generate the comparison tables (commit 7 configures this in `docs/make.jl`). On Julia 1.11, the 256-item "Manual vs. Recursive Unrolling" tests are skipped on every operating system, because JET can overflow the default stack while analyzing the recursive reference implementation.
3. [`89e12bc`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/89e12bc5ef35db32a6a8772c98eb27f088c84e3e) **fix: correctness bugs.** Start with `src/StaticBitVector.jl` (insert off-by-one, `drop` leaving stale words, promotion through `eltype_for_promotion`) and `src/StaticOneTo.jl`, then `src/unrollable_iterator_interface.jl` (`NamedTuple` constructor for both `NamedTuple{names}` and concrete `NamedTuple` types, which throws an `ArgumentError` when the number of items differs from the number of names; `Tuple` fallback in `output_promote_result`). `unrolled_take` and `unrolled_drop` throw a `BoundsError` for every out-of-range `N` and input type; for `NamedTuple`s, the items are sliced before the field names so that the error names the `NamedTuple`. `getindex` on a `StaticSequence` checks its index, `Iterators.reverse` of a `NamedTuple` reverses the field names, and `unrolled_product` builds `Tuple` combinations from `NamedTuple`s (`combination_output_type`). In `src/UnrolledUtilities.jl`, read the reductions (`unrolled_count`, `init` in `unrolled_sum`/`unrolled_prod`, `isless`/`isgreater` in `findmax`/`findmin`, `unrolled_unique` calling stateful callables once) and the recursion-limit block at the end of the file, which looks methods up by first-argument type. A new `Tuple` method of `unrolled_append` keeps `unrolled_flatten` and `unrolled_split` type-stable on heterogeneous tuples now that promotion looks at every item. `ext/UnrolledUtilitiesStaticArraysExt.jl` gets its own recursion-limit block for the extension's methods. New tests are in `test/container_and_callable.jl`.
4. [`95e4be5`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/95e4be50c9fd37e1c1ae7cbe84f6171277cab09a) **perf: compilation time.** `src/manually_unrolled_functions.jl` loses its `_unrolled_reduce` methods: `unrolled_reduce` is `unrolled_mapreduce` with `identity`, and internal reductions call a positional method of `_unrolled_mapreduce` that skips the keyword-argument method of `unrolled_mapreduce`. Functions of several iterators (`unrolled_map`, `unrolled_foreach`, `unrolled_mapreduce`, `unrolled_applyat`) call their callable through `splat_call`, a closure of this module, in place of `Base.splat`: the call method of `Base.Splat` cannot carry the module's recursion relation, so recursion through it is limited by the compiler's heuristic, which widened ClimaCore's nested tensor projections to `Any` (the downstream failure in `mul_with_projection`; a test modeled on it is in `test/container_and_callable.jl`). In `src/unrollable_iterator_interface.jl`, the error for inconsistent `output_promote_rule` methods is thrown from a `@noinline` function; a `@generated` function would infer as `Any` when the output types are not constants. The unused `⋅(f, ::Type)` method is removed. `src/UnrolledUtilities.jl` and `src/unrollable_iterator_interface.jl` gain:
   - ordinary methods in place of generated ones for `unrolled_map` on `Tuple`s and on `Zip`s of `Tuple`s, for `unrolled_flatten`, which appends pairwise in a balanced tree (as does `unrolled_append` of several iterators), and for the `Tuple` slices of `unrolled_partition`;
   - direct `unrolled_map` methods for two small `Tuple`s, `NamedTuple`s, and `StaticOneTo`, and `unrolled_foreach` methods for two small `Tuple`s;
   - splatting in `unrolled_append_into` for up to 32 items, output types computed without closures, and a `non_lazy_iterator` that returns `Tuple`s, `NamedTuple`s, `SVector`s, and `StaticBitVector`s unchanged.

   The unused `unrolled_map_output_type` is removed. Annotations stay as on `main`: the new `Tuple` methods of `unrolled_map` use `Base.@propagate_inbounds` like the existing ones, and all other new methods use `@inline`.
5. [`0243026`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/02430262b2f20e4841732f86321e8b9131c2423f) **perf: `StaticBitVector`.** In `src/StaticBitVector.jl`:
   - word-level `unrolled_map(!, bv)`, `any`/`all`/`count`, and `&`/`|` reductions (`unrolled_map(!, bv)` clears the unused bits of the last word, so its result is identical to `main`'s);
   - `unrolled_push`/`unrolled_append`/`ntuple` instead of tuple splats;
   - a constructor that accepts any callable and calls it once per bit;
   - constructors that clear the unused bits of the last word, so that vectors with the same bits are `===`, and a constructor from words that throws an `ArgumentError` unless it gets `cld(N, 8 * sizeof(U))` words.

   The GPU test width in `test/compilation_limits.jl` rises to 300 bits (38 words).
6. [`0b0b288`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/0b0b28816b011006be82cc1788a4fe5d373a7c16) **perf: `@inbounds` propagation.** All 42 exported functions and their internal helpers switch from `@inline` to `Base.@propagate_inbounds`, including `generic_getindex`, `getindex(::StaticSequence)`, the `_unrolled_*` functions, and the `StaticBitVector` methods. The closures and generated function bodies they use switch to `Base.@_propagate_inbounds_meta`, and callable arguments that are passed on to other functions get type parameters (the methods in `src/manually_unrolled_functions.jl` call them directly and stay unannotated). The checks of compile-time indices in `unrolled_take`, `unrolled_drop`, `unrolled_setindex`, and `unrolled_insert`, including their `StaticBitVector` and `StaticOneTo` methods, are `@boundscheck` blocks followed by `@inbounds` indexing, so `@inbounds` at the call site elides them. The functions that rearrange items read their inputs through `unrolled_map_into_tuple` in place of `ntuple`, whose closures do not propagate `@inbounds`, and the `StaticBitVector` methods read their words without bounds checks, which the word-count check of commit 5 makes safe.
7. [`c4ce8f4`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/c4ce8f441424db2ce9f86d2f738a45559905e5a2) **docs: documentation suite.** Each docstring gives the signature, a one-line summary naming the `Base` analogue, the behavior that differs from `Base`, one example, and cross-references. The module gets a docstring that `?UnrolledUtilities` shows. `docs/src/` gains `api.md` (shared container and `@inbounds` rules, a `Base`-to-unrolled table, and the `@docs` blocks), `cookbook.md`, and `limits.md`; `index.md` becomes a short landing page; the Introduction, User Guide, and Developer Guide get a clarity pass. Two small API additions live here because the docstrings and cookbook use them: a `StaticBitVector` constructor from a `Tuple` of `Bool`s with a matching `show` method, and an `ArgumentError` for reductions over empty iterators without `init`. `docs/make.jl` builds the tables by default (`UNROLLED_UTILITIES_BENCHMARK=false` skips them locally) and sets `checkdocs = :exports`.
8. [`39fe0a1`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/39fe0a13d05183dcb1306e7e26608bd3cf0b80af) **fix: widening in sums and products.** `unrolled_sum`, `unrolled_prod`, `unrolled_cumsum`, and `unrolled_cumprod` reduce with `Base.add_sum` and `Base.mul_prod`, and a new internal `reduction_first` passes the first item of a reduction without `init` through `Base.reduce_first` for these two operators only, so other operators are unaffected. Read `reduction_first` and the four functions in `src/UnrolledUtilities.jl`, the first-item branch of `unrolled_accumulate_into` in `src/StaticBitVector.jl`, and `_unrolled_accumulate_output_type` in `src/unrollable_iterator_interface.jl`, which infers the output container from the widened first item, or from `op(init, item)` when `init` is given. The docstrings of the four functions describe the widening. New tests are in `test/container_and_callable.jl`, including value-level constant folding of widened sums and products.
9. [`dd2ce07`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/dd2ce0750771c2b5590149be92b98b59c4cf0eb1) **chore: release 0.1.12.** `version = "0.1.12"` in `Project.toml` and a new `NEWS.md` with the changes of this PR.

## Changes

### Test dependencies ([`aa02501`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/aa0250101d1c5a4b0fa3bf4fdb0be487225c361f))

- `Project.toml` bounds `PrettyTables` to `"3"`, whose API the comparison-table printer in `test/test_and_analyze.jl` uses. The other test dependencies have no compat entries, so developers can test with newer versions. The bound only constrains the test and docs environments, so downstream packages are unaffected.
- **`gpu_broken` tests**: the 7 `gpu_broken` tests in `test/compilation_limits.jl` failed because of the test's own `runtime_int` helper, not the package: it boxed a `Float32` on the `InexactError` path of `Int(x)`. With `unsafe_trunc` in the helper, they pass with `main`'s package code.

### CI and benchmarks ([`81e5e55`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/81e5e557239644af87e7dd4a623ba8f92ac793eb))

- `UNROLLED_UTILITIES_BENCHMARK=true` enables the run-time and subprocess compile-time measurements in `@test_unrolled` and the comparison tables. Without it, each CI job runs the ~7800 tests in 7–16 minutes, including setup (34–53 minutes on `main`).
- Documentation builds generate the comparison tables on every event, including pull request previews, and take 30–40 minutes. `UNROLLED_UTILITIES_BENCHMARK=false` skips the benchmarks for local docs builds and writes only the section headings that other pages link to.
- Workflows use `setup-julia@v2`, `julia-actions/cache@v2`, concurrency groups, timeouts, and Documenter's recommended permissions. Benchmark subprocesses run the same Julia binary and project as the test process.

### Correctness ([`89e12bc`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/89e12bc5ef35db32a6a8772c98eb27f088c84e3e))

- **`StaticBitVector`**:
  - `unrolled_insert_into` inserted at `N + 1` and failed for `N == length(itr) + 1`. `unrolled_drop_into` left trailing words that corrupted later `push`/`append` calls. Both are fixed.
  - Lazy wrappers (`Iterators.reverse`, `Iterators.map`) and non-`Bool` items fall back to `Tuple` through a new `constructor_from_tuple` method and `eltype_for_promotion`. `eltype_for_promotion` replaces `first_item_type`/`second_item_type`, which also fixes promotion when a non-`Bool` appears after the first item.
  - `unrolled_take(::StaticOneTo, ::Val)` is bounds-checked, and `unrolled_take`/`unrolled_drop` throw a `BoundsError` (with the container and index) for every out-of-range `N`, where they threw an `ArgumentError` for some inputs and returned `(0, 1, 2, 3)` for `unrolled_drop(StaticOneTo(3), Val(-1))`.
  - In [`0243026`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/02430262b2f20e4841732f86321e8b9131c2423f): `StaticBitVector(true)` and `unrolled_take` left the unused bits of the last word set, so vectors with the same bits were not `===`, and the constructor from a `Tuple` of words accepted any number of words.
- **`NamedTuple`**: field names are preserved by every function that keeps the number of items (`unrolled_map`, `unrolled_setindex`, `unrolled_accumulate`, and so on) and by `unrolled_take`, `unrolled_drop`, and `unrolled_partition`. Functions that would change the number of items (`push`, `insert`, `filter`, `unique`, `split`, `append` of two `NamedTuple`s with the same names) throw an `ArgumentError` that suggests `Tuple(nt)` or `values(nt)`, so the output type never depends on the values of a predicate. `Iterators.reverse` of a `NamedTuple` reverses its field names, and the combinations in `unrolled_product` are `Tuple`s. `output_promote_result` returns `Tuple` for container pairs without a rule.
- **`getindex`** on `StaticOneTo` and `StaticBitVector` returned values for out-of-range indices (`StaticOneTo(3)[5] == 5`); it throws a `BoundsError`.
- **Reductions**:
  - `unrolled_count` on one item returned `Bool`.
  - `unrolled_sum`/`unrolled_prod` ignored `init` on non-empty input.
  - `findmax`/`findmin`/`argmax`/`argmin` now compare with `isless` and an `isgreater` that is equivalent to `Base.isgreater`. They match `Base` for `NaN`, `missing`, and signed zeros, including inputs that contain both `NaN` and `missing`. `Base.isgreater` itself is not used, because with it Julia 1.10 cannot infer `unrolled_argmin` on the wide heterogeneous input of `test/compilation_limits.jl`.
  - `unrolled_unique`/`unrolled_allunique` call non-singleton callables once per item.
  - In [`39fe0a1`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/39fe0a13d05183dcb1306e7e26608bd3cf0b80af): `unrolled_sum`, `unrolled_prod`, `unrolled_cumsum`, and `unrolled_cumprod` reduced with `+` and `*`, so `unrolled_sum(Int8.((100, 100)))` overflowed to `-56` and `unrolled_cumsum((true, true, true))` returned `(true, 2, 3)`. They now widen `Bool`s and integers narrower than `Int` to `Int`s or `UInt`s, as `Base.sum`, `Base.prod`, `Base.cumsum`, and `Base.cumprod` do, giving `200` and `(1, 2, 3)`. `unrolled_cumsum` of a `StaticBitVector` returns a `Tuple` of `Int`s (as it already did for more than one item), and `unrolled_cumprod` of a `StaticBitVector` returns a `StaticBitVector`. With an `init`, `unrolled_accumulate` infers its output container from `op(init, item)`, so a `StaticBitVector` stays a `StaticBitVector` for any `init` when `op` returns `Bool`s.
- **Recursion limits**: every method defined in the module has its recursion limit removed via `Base._methods_by_ftype`. This covers closures, constructors, `Core.kwcall`, and this module's methods for `Base` functions, and it works on Julia 1.10 through 1.12. The StaticArrays extension also removes the limits of its own methods.

### Performance ([`95e4be5`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/95e4be50c9fd37e1c1ae7cbe84f6171277cab09a), [`0243026`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/02430262b2f20e4841732f86321e8b9131c2423f), [`0b0b288`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/0b0b28816b011006be82cc1788a4fe5d373a7c16))

- **Compilation time**: compiling `test/compilation_limits.jl`, which builds the exported functions for a 60-item tuple of 22 types on CPU and GPU, allocates 25% less at commit 4 than at commit 3, and 34% less at the final commit (Julia 1.11: 203 M → 155 M → 134 M allocations; 1.10: 148 M → 109 M → 96 M). On 1.11, its "baseline: wide and heterogenous inputs" testset runs 1.5x faster from commit 3 to commit 4, in 5.6 s instead of 8.2 s (two runs each; 1.10 run times vary too much between runs on this machine to compare). The changes are:
  - a positional `_unrolled_mapreduce` method for internal reductions, with `unrolled_reduce` defined as `unrolled_mapreduce` with `identity`;
  - ordinary methods in place of the generated ones for `unrolled_map` on `Tuple`s and `Zip`s, `unrolled_flatten`, and `unrolled_partition`;
  - direct `unrolled_map` and `unrolled_foreach` methods for small `Tuple`s, `NamedTuple`s, and `StaticOneTo`;
  - output types computed without closures.
- **Word-level `StaticBitVector`** implementations of `unrolled_map(!, bv)`, `unrolled_any`, `unrolled_all`, `unrolled_count`, and `&`/`|` reductions. Measured on a `StaticBitVector{256}` with Julia 1.11, commit 4 → commit 5:
  - the first call, including compilation, is 7x–35x faster (for example, 0.85 s → 0.024 s for `unrolled_count(bv)`);
  - on an A100, kernels in which each of 2^22 threads loads a 256-bit vector from global memory run 1.2x faster for `unrolled_count` and the `&`/`|` reductions (360–376 μs → 300 μs), and 3.1x faster for `unrolled_any` and `unrolled_all` (358 μs → 116 μs).
- **Beyond 32 words**: no tuple splats remain in `StaticBitVector`, so 300-bit vectors compile and run without allocations on CPU and GPU.
- **`@inbounds` propagation**: all 42 exported functions propagate `@inbounds` from the call site to iterator indexing, and to user callables marked with `Base.@propagate_inbounds`. Checks of compile-time indices, such as `N` in `unrolled_take(itr, Val(N))`, are `@boundscheck` blocks that `@inbounds` elides. Measured in fresh processes on a 60-item heterogeneous `Tuple` (median of 5 runs), this cuts the first call on Julia 1.10 from 33 to 27 ms for `unrolled_take`, 34 to 28 ms for `unrolled_drop`, 47 to 38 ms for `unrolled_setindex`, 50 to 40 ms for `unrolled_insert`, and 34 to 24 ms for `unrolled_take` under `@inbounds`; on 1.11 the times are unchanged within 1 ms.
  - On `main`, only `unrolled_map` on `Tuple`s propagated.
  - Measured on an A100 with Julia 1.11 at the previous revision of commits 5 and 6, for kernels that apply each function under `@inbounds` to 8 values read through a `Base.@propagate_inbounds` accessor over a `CuDeviceArray`:

  | Kernel | PTX lines | `throw_boundserror` calls | Time (μs) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `unrolled_sum` | 172 → 61 | 8 → 0 | 116.7 → 116.7 |
  | `unrolled_maximum` | 172 → 61 | 8 → 0 | 116.7 → 115.7 |
  | `unrolled_findmax` | 256 → 159 | 8 → 0 | 118.8 → 117.8 |
  | `unrolled_count` | 189 → 78 | 8 → 0 | 116.7 → 116.7 |
  | `unrolled_findfirst` | 196 → 101 | 8 → 0 | 115.7 → 115.7 |
  | `unrolled_mapreduce` | 172 → 61 | 8 → 0 | 117.8 → 116.7 |
  | `unrolled_any` | 190 → 95 | 8 → 0 | 115.7 → 115.7 |

  Run times do not change because these kernels are memory-bound.

### Documentation ([`c4ce8f4`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/c4ce8f441424db2ce9f86d2f738a45559905e5a2))

- Pages: Home (installation, a quick example that runs during the build and shows `Base`'s type instability and allocations next to the unrolled results, and a table of contents), Introduction, User Guide, Cookbook, Compilation Limits, API Reference, Developer Guide, and Comparison Tables.
  - The **Cookbook** has five recipes that run during the build: transforming `NamedTuple` fields and filtering their values, computing a type parameter from a filtered `Tuple`, indexing a heterogeneous `Tuple` with a run-time index, reading an array through a `Base.@propagate_inbounds` closure without bounds checks, and updating a `StaticBitVector` bitmask in a loop.
  - **Compilation Limits** documents what `test/compilation_limits.jl` checks: loop lengths must be known during compilation, predicates with run-time values keep a `Union` only up to two or three item types, recursion limits of `Base` functions cannot be lifted, and GPU error paths need constant messages. Each limit has an executed example or a link.
  - The **API Reference** opens with a table from `Base` and `Iterators` names to the unrolled functions, states the shared container-type and `@inbounds` rules once, and renders every docstring in `@docs` blocks. `checkdocs = :exports` fails the build on undocumented exports.
- Every exported function and type has a docstring with its signature, a one-line summary naming the `Base` analogue, the behavior that differs from `Base`, one example, and cross-references. The module docstring lists the functions by category for `?UnrolledUtilities`.
- `StaticBitVector` can be constructed from a `Tuple` of `Bool`s and prints as that constructor call, so REPL output and test failures show the bits. Reductions over empty iterators without `init` throw an `ArgumentError` whose message applies to every reduction function.
- The README gains installation instructions, a quick example, a table of exported operations, and links to the new pages. The badge table gains a version row backed by the GitHub tag badge, which tracks the `v0.1.x` tags that TagBot creates; JuliaHub's badge endpoint returns HTTP 502 for every package at the moment.
- Downstream: ClimaAtmos pins `UnrolledUtilities = "0.1.9"`, so it receives these fixes only after its compat is bumped; CompatHelper opens that PR once 0.1.12 is registered.

### Review comments

Responses to the review of the previous revision, each folded into the commit named above:

- `fused_mapreduce` is a positional method of `_unrolled_mapreduce`, `unrolled_reduce` is `unrolled_mapreduce` with `identity`, and the `_unrolled_reduce` methods and the callable annotations in `src/manually_unrolled_functions.jl` are gone (commits 4 and 6). First-call times of the reductions on a 60-item heterogeneous `Tuple` are unchanged on 1.10 and 1.11.
- The `SVector` methods of `unrolled_map` and `unrolled_foreach` in the extension were equivalent to the generic methods; removing them changes no first-call time by more than 2 ms on either Julia version, so the `Tuple` conversions are not moved into `src` (commit 4).
- `NamedTuple` outputs error instead of falling back to `Tuple` when the number of items changes (commit 3).
- The inconsistent-promotion error is thrown from a `@noinline` function (commit 4). The `@generated` version of the previous revision inferred as `Any` for non-constant output types, which the downstream ClimaCore tests caught.
- Compile-time index checks are `@boundscheck` blocks (commit 6); see the measurements under "Performance".
- Only `PrettyTables` keeps a compat entry among the test dependencies (commit 1).
- Docs: the `StaticBitVector` rule, the constant-folding paragraph, the `Symbol` remark on the Compilation Limits page, the home-page and README examples, the `NamedTuple` and bounds-check recipes (an annotated closure instead of a struct; `unrolled_sum(abs, state)` and `values(state)` instead of `Tuple(state)` and `select`), and the README's features and table (commit 7).
- The downstream ClimaCore failure in `mul_with_projection` was a recursion-limit regression of the fused `unrolled_mapreduce` over several iterators, present since commit 4 of the first revision and exposed by ClimaCore tests added since: `Base.splat` is replaced by a closure of this module (commit 4), with a regression test. ClimaCore's `mul_with_projection` unit tests pass locally on 1.10 with this revision (224 tests), fail with the previous one, and pass with `main`.
- A final review pass added the `getindex` bounds check, the `NamedTuple` fixes for `Iterators.reverse` and `unrolled_product`, the accumulate-with-`init` output type, and the removal of the unused `⋅` method listed above, and shortened the lines and comments that the code-comment sweep flagged.
- `methods(f)` looks up `Tuple{Core.Typeof(f), Vararg}`, so it needs an instance; a closure type with captured variables has none, and `methods(C)` returns the constructors of `C`. `main` reached closure call methods through `C.name.mt`, which Julia 1.12 removed. `Base._methods_by_ftype` takes the signature type directly, so one lookup covers functions, closure types, and constructors on 1.10 through 1.12.

## Release ([`dd2ce07`](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/commit/dd2ce0750771c2b5590149be92b98b59c4cf0eb1))

Nothing in this PR is breaking, so it bumps the patch version (0.1.11 → 0.1.12) rather than the minor version:

- The exports, the `julia` and `StaticArrays` compat bounds, and the package dependencies are unchanged. All 71 exported method signatures of v0.1.11, including keyword arguments, still dispatch.
- Every behavior change relative to v0.1.11 is a bug fix (for example, `unrolled_sum(itr; init)` no longer ignores `init`) or a call that threw an error and now returns a result (for example, most functions on `NamedTuple`s).
- Sums and products of `Bool`s and integers narrower than `Int` return `Int`s or `UInt`s, where they returned the narrower type and could overflow. The docstrings describe these functions as analogues of `sum`, `prod`, `cumsum`, and `cumprod`, which widen, so this is treated as a bug fix.
- Downstream packages (ClimaCore and others) use only exported functions and `UnrolledUtilities.unrolled_map_into_tuple`, whose signature is unchanged. None of them extend the unrollable iterator interface.

`NEWS.md` is new and follows the [CliMA changelog guide](https://github.com/CliMA/DeveloperGuides/blob/main/code-quality/changelogs_and_versions.md), with an empty `main` section above `v0.1.12`. The guide puts releases in their own PR, so commit 9 can also be dropped here and moved to a separate release PR.

## Testing

Run locally on Julia 1.10.11 and 1.11.9 with a freshly resolved test environment (CUDA.jl 6.4.1, GPUCompiler 2.9.0, JET 0.9.18 on 1.10 and 0.9.20 on 1.11, PrettyTables 3.5.0, Aqua 0.8.18). The GPU tests compile for an sm_80 target.

- **Full suite**: `Pkg.test(; coverage = false)` on a clean checkout of the final commit passes on both 1.10 (7853 tests) and 1.11 (7801 tests), with no failures or errors; the regression test for the recursion through `unrolled_mapreduce` was added after that run and passes with `test/container_and_callable.jl` on both versions at every commit from 4 on. In the previous revision, every commit was run on both versions (1.10: 7703, 7703, 7774, 7779, 7812, 7812, 7817, 7834, 7834; 1.11: 7795, 7651, 7722, 7727, 7760, 7760, 7765, 7782, 7782). In this revision, commits 4–9 were re-run with `test/container_and_callable.jl` and `test/aqua.jl` on 1.10 and 1.11 (commits 1–3 are unchanged from the previous revision); commit 9 has the tree that the full suite was run on. On 1.11, the counts are lower than on 1.10 because the 256-item cases of "Manual vs. Recursive Unrolling" are skipped on every operating system.
- **Test organization**: each commit adds the tests in `test/container_and_callable.jl` for its own changes. The "@inbounds propagation" testset of the previous revision is removed. `Pkg.test` runs with `--check-bounds=yes`, so that testset could not detect whether `@inbounds` propagates. The results it compared are already covered by `test/test_and_analyze.jl`.
- **`@inbounds` and constant folding** (1.11): a local script checks whether `@inbounds` at the call site reaches the indexing of an iterator whose bounds check throws. It does in all 42 exported functions at commits 6 and 7, and in none at commits 3–5. Another script checks that a `StaticBitVector` with too few words throws an `ArgumentError` from commit 5 on; before this revision, `unrolled_push` on such a vector crashed the Julia process at commit 6. Value-level constant folding held in all 26 checked cases at the previous revision, and commit 8 adds tests that the widened sums and products fold.
- **Docs and formatting**: at commit 9, `julia --project=docs/ docs/make.jl` builds with `checkdocs = :exports` on 1.11, as in the Documentation workflow, and the README example runs on 1.10 and 1.11. JuliaFormatter reports no changes at any commit. The 78 examples in the docstrings evaluate to the results stated in their comments, and a full docs build, with benchmarks, generates all seven comparison tables.
